records.title: U.S. Army Flight Physiology Program
records.locator: Aviation, Space, and Environmental Medicine 67(6), p. 602
records.evidence_note: The chief of Flight Physiology at USASAM reports that approximately 60,000 aircrew members had been trained at the Fort Rucker chamber since its establishment in 1971. The report supplies no DCS case count, repeat-entry rule, staff exposure count or post-training ascertainment. The cumulative period overlaps the published historical Army series.

records.title: USASAM tests decompression sickness MedEvac procedures
records.locator: Army Flier, 13 August 2015, printed p. A3
records.evidence_note: The July 31 exercise used a simulated patient. The publication also says more than 67,000 aircrew members had been trained since the chamber began in 1971. The period overlaps Thompson and includes the start of the Vargo ascertainment period. The cumulative count cannot be subtracted from the earlier approximate count to estimate exact interim exposures.

records.title: NAMI Hyperbarics conducts joint exercise with Fort Novosel
records.evidence_note: The Navy documents an Army–Navy hyperbaric DCS exercise and simulated patient loading. The record provides no real DCS diagnoses and no chamber cohort.

records.title: DCS Incidence and Reporting, Session Four Discussion 5
records.evidence_note: Weien described about 12 regular rotating chamber staff plus occasional participants. Asked about career consequences of reporting Type II disease, he confirmed that it could end technician duties and that one technician was grounded. This establishes a potential reporting incentive and a clustered staff exposure pattern. Unreported case numbers and staff person-exposure totals remain unknown.

records.title: Heart rate, blood pressure, and SpO2 responses to simulated 5000 m hypobaric exposure in healthy male Vietnamese pilots
records.evidence_note: Seventy-five healthy male pilots attended as part of routine altitude chamber training at the Vietnam Institute of Aviation Medicine in 2024.
